title: The fr run cursor tells the truth about what it is waiting for (gh-499, gh-501, gh-500, gh-496)
body:
Fixes #499, #501, #500, #496 — the `fr run` cursor cluster filed 2026-09-20, as one PR.

- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-20-fr-run-cursor-cluster-design.md`
- Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-20-fr-run-cursor-cluster/` (7 phases; phase 7 is `[manual]`)
- Version: **4.8.0 → 4.9.0** (minor — two new CLI flags and a mandatory new refusal)

## ⛔ Ready-checklist guard — do not merge while this section is present

- [ ] CI green on this branch
- [ ] Explicit review OK from the operator
- [ ] No commits pushed since that OK

`gh pr ready` is run only when all three hold, and this section is removed in the same act.

## What was wrong, and the one shape behind it

Four reports, one shape: **the cursor knew more than it said.** Two of them are narrowings — a
richer upstream fact discarded exactly where it would have been load-bearing.

| # | Symptom | Where the fact already existed |
|---|---|---|
| #499 | `advance` re-emitted a **byte-identical** brief for a `kind: agent` step already `running` | `fr run status` printed `phase/2/implement-phase: running` |
| #501 | `advance` printed a composite id that `resolve --step` rejected as "not found in workflow" | the JSON brief beside it already carried `step` and `item` separately |
| #500 | `fr run start` bound no session, so every fr-goal workspace read `sessions=none` | `fr isolation attach` existed and repaired it mid-flight |
| #496 | `for_each: phase` built a brief for a `tag: manual` phase | `_group_phases` parsed the plan carrying `tag`, then returned bare numbers |

#499 is the one with teeth: fr-goal dispatches phase executors into the **one** isolation
worktree that already exists, and `isolation: "worktree"` is forbidden for them by design
(#420) — so the usual two-agents-one-tree protection is deliberately unavailable, and a second
brief means two executors editing the same files and committing to the same branch.

**#500 reproduced itself.** The first command of the run that produced this PR created a
workspace `fr isolation status` immediately reported as `sessions=none`.

## The design decision worth reading

**#496 was reframed by the operator during the batched Q&A**, and it reshaped the fix. The
options on the table were all *runtime behaviours* — skip it, record it, or add a `deferred`
resolve state. The operator asked why a manual phase should be in a `for_each` at all, which
turns it into a *structural* question: **where may a manual phase sit?**

An invariant can be checked before anything runs; a behaviour can only be observed at dispatch.
So the primary enforcement is `severity="error"` in `fr.plan_ops.self_review` — which fr-goal
already runs as its `plan-review` step, a `kind: cli` step whose exit code is the verdict. A
mis-shaped plan now fails **before phase 1 is ever dispatched**. The run model's job shrank to
"never build a brief, never hide the omission".

The rule is *no manual phase may be **outstanding** when an agentic phase after it runs* —
trailing block, **or** already `plan_locally_complete`:

```
VALID   1 agentic, 2 agentic, 3 agentic, 4 [manual]           back-loaded (fr-goal §3 default)
VALID   1 agentic, 2 agentic, 3 [manual], 4 [manual]          a trailing BLOCK, not just one
VALID   1 [manual] (ticked), 2 agentic depends_on [1]         front-loaded, go given (fr-goal §3)
ERROR   1 agentic, 2 [manual] (unticked), 3 agentic           phase 3 would wait on a human
```

**This was measured before it was written** (spec §1.4): **4/4 live plans, 80/80 archived plans
and 16/16 fixture plan folders** already satisfy it. Zero exceptions. The rule codifies how this
repo already writes plans rather than imposing a new constraint — which rewrote the risk
assessment the spec had first made from speculation.

## Dogfooded on its own run

This plan's phase 7 is a trailing `[manual]` phase, so the fix had to work for this PR to exist.
After phase 5, the fan-out shrank from 14 units to 12 and the live cursor reads:

```
implement: done (12 members done; phase 7 `tag: manual`, never dispatched — the plan's own steps and the PR are its record)
```

Before this PR, `fr run advance` would have handed an agent a dispatch brief for a phase whose
steps are *"run a paid `/fr-goal` on your own machine"*.

## Findings — 9, all closed

Every one was fixed with a test; none was dropped or argued away.

| id | phase | finding |
|---|---|---|
| `p1-f1` | 1 | `_advance_group` printed its JSON brief **without** `soft_wrap`, so rich folded it at 80 columns whenever stdout is piped — `tail -1` got a fragment. No test caught it, because the inserted newline is legal inter-token JSON whitespace. |
| `r1-f1` | 1 | The resolve hint ended `--state done\|failed`, which **is not pasteable**: `\|` is a shell pipe, so pasting runs the resolve with `--state done` and then exits 127 on `command not found: failed` — reporting failure over a run whose state already moved. The defect class this PR removes, reintroduced by the hint that teaches the fix. The test now *pastes* the line (lifts it off stdout, `shlex.split`s it, runs it). |
| `r1-f2` | 1 | The new composite-id refusal rendered through the one `err_console.print` in `resolve_cmd` lacking `soft_wrap`. |
| `p2-f1` | 2 | An existing test **pinned the #499 bug as the contract** (`test_advance_agent_step_brief_is_re_emitted_idempotently_while_running`). Rewritten, not deleted. A second one did not go red when it should have — it passed for the wrong reason for one commit. |
| `p3-f1` | 3 | `fr-goal/SKILL.md` was sitting exactly **on** its 120-line ceiling, so "add two sentences" cost two test failures. |
| `r4-f1` | 4 | The `depends_on` half was unconditional over every manual phase, which **made fr-goal §3's front-load shape unexpressible** — front-loading is *defined* by that dependency. Both halves now key on *outstanding*. The defect was in the phase brief, not the executor's work; it flagged the corner rather than softening the rule. |
| `p5-f1` | 5 | The new markers made `fr run adopt` count un-dispatchable work as outstanding (`2/4` for a plan whose phase 4 can never be dispatched) — #496's own narrowing, reintroduced by the fix for #496. |
| `p1-f2` | 1 → 6 | Three suite failures, **verified pre-existing** (CI green on `main`; the branch never touched those files). Operator-scoped into phase 6. Both root causes fixed; see below. |

Full text: `fr journal render --scope plan --slug 2026-09-20-fr-run-cursor-cluster --section findings`.

## Decisions (operator, batched Q&A)

`d1` exit 2 + `--redispatch` · `d2` teach the flag rather than accept the composite · `d3` bind
on all three surfaces · **`d4` manual placement is structural, enforced at authoring** · **`d5`
front-loading survives as "trailing OR already complete"** · `d6` the trailing block stays
outside the cursor's step list · `d7` the Test Plan ships as a back-loaded `[manual]` phase ·
`d8` (mid-flight) `p1-f2`'s two root causes scoped into this PR.

Full text: `fr journal render --scope spec --slug 2026-09-20-fr-run-cursor-cluster --section decisions`.

## Operator gates

```
brainstorm: operator gate answered by the operator
```

Verbatim from `fr run gates 2026-09-20-fix-fr-run-cursor-cluster`. The one gate this shape
declares was answered by a human, not cleared by the agent.

## Scope taken on deliberately (`d8`)

Phase 1 surfaced three Mac-only suite failures that predate the branch. Neither
`fr journal resolve --state` value — `fixed` or `refuted` — is honest for "real, but not here",
so an open finding would have blocked `deliver` with no truthful way to close it. The operator
chose to fix both causes here:

1. **`fr run start`'s refusal printed without `soft_wrap`** — rich folded it and the assertion
   straddled the break. Fixed in the **source**, not the test: `git diff` on
   `tests/unit/test_run_workspace.py` against `main` is **empty**, so both assertions stand
   byte-unchanged. It is the same defect class as `p1-f1` and `r1-f2`, one function away.
2. **`test_cli_all_fails_when_nothing_is_discoverable` monkeypatched 3 of 4 sources** — the
   fourth, the marketplace clone under `$HOME`, made a test asserting "nothing is discoverable"
   pass on a host where something was.

The suite is now **0 failed** on macOS, where it was 3.

## Scope declined deliberately

- **`x3`** — the hooks pass `--harness claude`, but `fr.harness.HARNESSES` and `fr models` say
  `claude-code`. Pre-existing; the value is only ever *written*, never read for behaviour, so
  nothing is broken. Phase 3 makes `--harness` operator-facing for the first time, so it is
  worth knowing. One word in two hooks whenever the label should be trustworthy.
- **`x6`** — a third instance of the `soft_wrap` class at `run_cmd.py:1595` (the generic
  "not a phase member" refusal), which interpolates a list whose length grows with the plan.
  Predates this PR and is outside `d8`'s two named causes.
- `test_render_deps.py:323` builds a non-compliant manual-phase shape, and was **left alone**:
  it never reaches `self_review`, and rewriting a render fixture to satisfy an authoring gate it
  does not call would be ceremony. Weakening the rule for it was never on the table.

## Acceptance matrix

Five rows **added** by this work (`fr acceptance check --added-since origin/main`), each
`not-implemented` at brainstorm and flipped to `ci` by the phase that landed its evidence:

| row | one-line defense |
|---|---|
| `run-advance-refuses-running` | The claim is about what the operator is *told* when re-entering cold, not about a state check. |
| `run-resolve-teaches-item-flag` | Fires once per phase per run; a usability contract, not a string format. |
| `run-start-binds-session` | Observability of unattended runs — the binding's entire purpose. |
| `plan-manual-phase-trailing` | A doctrine claim about *when* the refusal lands: authoring, not mid-run. |
| `run-manual-phase-never-dispatched` | Both halves matter — silence about a deliberate skip is the same defect class as a false dispatch. |

Standing debt is unchanged by this PR: `ci: 107, skipped: 18, not-implemented: 4`. The `skipped`
rows are pre-existing backfill owed and are not made worse here.

## Phase 7 — unimplemented; operator pushes to this PR

Phase 7 is the back-loaded `[manual]` live-verification phase, fr-goal's documented default. It
**ships unimplemented**: its steps are unticked and no agent was ever offered them. Its steps
cost a real, paid `/fr-goal` run on a real machine.

### Test Plan (post-merge, operator-driven) — verbatim from spec §5

Automated coverage lands in CI per phase. These four need a real run, because three of the four
bugs were found by *running* the pipeline: every unit fixture creates its runs in the workspace
and so satisfies the assumptions by construction — the same blind spot that produced the
`_existing_run_for_workflow` bug.

1. **#499 live** — start an `/fr-goal` run, let `implement` dispatch a phase executor, and call `fr run advance` again mid-flight. Expect the ALREADY RUNNING refusal and exit 2; then `--redispatch` and confirm it re-briefs the same unit and no other.
2. **#501 live** — paste the composite id into `resolve --step` and confirm the error teaches the two flags; confirm `advance`'s hint line precedes the JSON and that `tail -1` still yields parseable JSON.
3. **#500 live** — `fr run start` on a fresh branch in Claude Code, then `fr isolation status`: expect `sessions=<uuid>`, not `sessions=none`. Repeat with the hook disabled and the explicit `--session` flag.
4. **#496 live** — run a plan whose last phase is `[manual]` (this plan is one) and confirm: no brief is built for it, `fr run status` shows `phase/<n>: manual`, `implement` completes, and `deliver` still opens the PR. Then author a plan with a *middle* unticked manual phase and confirm `fr plan self-review` fails it with the §D.1 message.

## Verification (run in the workspace, not quoted from a subagent)

| gate | verdict |
|---|---|
| `uv run pytest` (full form, coverage exercised) | `3330 passed, 80 skipped` — **0 failed**; `Required test coverage of 75% reached. Total coverage: 91.76%` |
| `uv run ruff check packages/ tests/` | `All checks passed!` |
| `uv run mypy` (4 src trees) | `Success: no issues found in 138 source files` |
| `uv run fr acceptance check` | `129 rows OK` |
| `uv run fr harness parity --check` | `declared matrix agrees with the registration files` |
| `uv run fr validate artifacts` | `33 artifact(s) checked — all structurally valid` |
| `uv run python scripts/sync-opencode.py --check` | `.opencode/ mirrors are in sync.` |
| `uv run python scripts/sync-hermes.py --check` | `.hermes/ mirrors are in sync.` |
| `uv run fr journal check --scope plan` | clean (all findings closed) |
| `uv run fr plan self-review <plan>` | `self-review passed` |
| `uv run --no-project python scripts/bump-version.py --check` | `ok — versions agree` (10 surfaces at 4.9.0) |

The explainer was regenerated, not hand-edited: the **unmodified** page was re-rendered first and
`cmp`'d byte-identical against the committed `.html` to pin the renderer, and the real render's
diff contains only the three passages written.
